properties.label: St. Paul Water Company canal, Lambert Lake to Vadnais
properties.note: The 1886 plate draws a narrow strip with its own acreages (1.37, 0.10, 0.26, 1.69, 0.32 a.) cut across private parcels from the south-west shore of Lambert Lake to East Vadnais: a right-of-way, read here as the water company's 1870 conduit. The strip centre-line was traced on the plate. Within about 30 m of the modern channel along its length. Oriented lake to Vadnais.
sources: Warner & Foote, History of Ramsey County and the City of St. Paul (1881), pp. 281, 434
St. Paul Board of Water Commissioners report (1891): right-of-way award Vadnais-Lambert, filed 4 May 1870
G. M. Hopkins, Atlas of Ramsey County (1886), plate with sec. 29-32 T30N R22W

properties.label: A. K. Barnum's ditch, 5,963 ft, along the abandoned conduit
properties.traced_from: OSM waterway + LiDAR low line, cut to the court-record length
properties.note: Swank v. Barnum gives the length (5,963 ft = 1,818 m) and says it followed the abandoned conduit. The line is the modern channel from East Vadnais back along the conduit's valley (1,409 m to the 1847 shore, matching the 1886 strip) and then 409 m north-east into the lake bed along the straight ditch line, cut at 1,818 m. The valley reach is good; where the ditch ended in the bed, and whether the straight reach is Barnum's alignment, is inferred. 1,776 + 1,970 ft was covered sluice, location not stated.
sources: G. M. Hopkins, Atlas of Ramsey County (1886), plate with sec. 29-32 T30N R22W

properties.label: Ramsey County Ditch 14 (Lambert Creek)
properties.note: The main ditch through the bed: from where Lambert Creek crosses the 1847 east shore at Hwy 61 / County Rd E, past the pond site, straight south-west across the bed, then down the old conduit valley to East Vadnais. Where the 2021 meander now runs, the line is the straight ditch seen in the 1940 and 2017 air photos. The 1940 photo is the earliest image of it; the 1916 route is assumed to be the 1940 route. County Ditch 13 is not located (no map found).

properties.label: Lateral, west ring (north-south, then south-east to the main ditch)
properties.note: Straight ditch with spoil bank, clear on the 1940 photo; still mapped in OSM. Lateral number unknown (the 1927 system was Nos. 1, 1A, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5A, 5B).

properties.label: Lateral, west ring branch
properties.note: In OSM; faint on the 1940 photo. Attribution to 1927 is inferred.

properties.label: Lateral, north (north-north-west from the pond site)
properties.note: Straight dark line on the 1940 photo; in OSM. Could equally be part of Ditch 13 or 14; attribution to the 1927 laterals is inferred.

properties.label: Lambert Lake Pond
properties.note: Built 2002-05 under a Clean Water Partnership grant with a 530-ft overflow dam to spread flow into the wetland.
sources: MPCA 2008 watershed achievements report (Clean Water Partnership, Lambert Lake)

properties.label: Lambert Creek meander restoration
properties.traced_from: OSM waterway, checked on 2024 air photo
properties.note: Built Jan-Feb 2021 by SEH for VLAWMO, about 2,020 ft, replacing the straight ditch reach between the pond and the south-west bed.
sources: Star Tribune, May 2020, "Crews reshape Ramsey County creek"

properties.label: Lambert Creek today
properties.note: Today's channel from the 1847 east shore (Hwy 61 / County Rd E) to East Vadnais, including the 2021 meander. Oriented upstream to downstream.
